text: 2012. Night map of Ukraine and its neighbours. The Black Sea and Sea of Azov are dark at the bottom, with Crimea between them. Moscow is the largest bright cluster, at the top right. Other bright clusters include Warsaw on the left, Kyiv in the centre, Kharkiv and Dnipro to the east and south-east, and Odesa on the coast. Many smaller towns are scattered between them.

2023. The same view as 2012. Several bright clusters in the centre and east look smaller and dimmer than in 2012, including Kyiv, Kharkiv, Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia and the coast near Odesa. Moscow, Warsaw and Bucharest look brighter.

Change map, 2012 to 2023. The same view in dim colours. Purple marks places that look brighter in 2023 than in 2012, and orange marks places that look dimmer. Purple dominates around Moscow, Warsaw and Bucharest. Orange covers many cities in central and eastern Ukraine, including Kyiv, Kharkiv, Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia and Odesa. In the west, Poland and western Ukraine show a mix of purple and small orange specks.
